item.title: Hunter Biden Blames Cancer for Joe Biden’s Disastrous Debate
item.description: Medical experts say it is unlikely that Mr. Biden’s debate performance was affected by the cancer that was diagnosed months later.
item.dc:creator: Reid J. Epstein and Nina Agrawal
item.media:credit: Alyssa Schukar for The New York Times
item.media:description: Former President Joseph R. Biden Jr. at an event in Washington last year.

item.title: Trump Administration Plans to Upend Head Start by Deregulating It
item.description: The White House tried but failed to block funding for preschool for poor children. Instead, it will seek to strip away standards on health, literacy — and brushing teeth.
item.dc:creator: Coral Davenport
item.media:description: A teacher at a Head Start program run by Easterseals South Florida instructing students on reading and writing. Head Start has served over 30 million children since it was created.

item.title: John Ali, Nation of Islam Official Who Clashed With Malcolm X, Dies at 98
item.description: He was widely suspected of being an F.B.I. informant and of playing a role in the 1965 assassination of Malcolm, the charismatic Black activist.
item.dc:creator: Clay Risen
item.media:description: Jon Ali, back row center, the Nation of Islam’s de facto second-in-command, stands behind the group’s leader, Elijah Muhammad, between Jabir Herbert Muhammad, left, Mr. Muhammad’s son, and James Shabazz, minister of the Nation’s mosque in Newark, during a news conference after the assassination of Malcolm X in February 1965.

item.title: Why Mitch McConnell Isn’t Giving Up His Senate Seat
item.description: Democrats are demanding that the Kentucky Republican resign. Others who were sidelined for far longer faced no such calls, but times are changing.
item.dc:creator: Carl Hulse
item.media:description: Senator Mitch McConnell heading to a vote in May.

item.title: Nancy Guthrie Ransom Notes Released by Sheriff’s Department Searching for New Leads
item.description: The 84-year-old mother of Savannah Guthrie, the television news anchor, has been missing for nearly six months.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Bogel-Burroughs
item.media:description: A memorial near the driveway to Nancy Guthrie’s residence in February in Tucson, Ariz.

item.title: Trump Blames Minnesota, Not Iran, for Cyberattack, Despite Initial Investigation
item.description: President Trump claimed without evidence that Minnesota’s Democratic government was “behind” a cyberattack on the state’s own water systems. Investigators believe Iran is likely responsible.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Eric Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: Gov. Tim Walz of Minnesota said President Trump’s attempt to blame him for the cyberattack “further illustrates there’s no plan to win a war with Iran.”

item.title: Trump to Appeal Judge’s Ruling Denouncing I.R.S. Lawsuit as Exercise in Self-Dealing
item.description: It was the latest sign that the president was doubling down on his fight for aspects of a deal that brings him vast benefits, even though they have jeopardized the confirmation of his pick for attorney general.
item.dc:creator: Alan Feuer and Andrew Duehren
item.media:description: President Trump reiterated his support for the so-called anti-weaponization fund in a social media post on Friday.

item.title: Trump Escalates Feud With Senate Over Blanche
item.description: The president’s comments threw the confirmation of Todd Blanche, his pick to be attorney general, further into doubt.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold
item.media:credit: Pete Marovich for The New York Times
item.media:description: Todd Blanche, the acting attorney general, during a cabinet meeting at Camp David on Friday.

item.title: Driver Fatally Shoots Kidnapped Victim in Trunk in Chino Hills
item.description: An abduction from a home in Chino Hills led to a short police chase. The driver fired at a man in the trunk before being gunned down.
item.dc:creator: Orlando Mayorquín and Vik Jolly
item.media:description: The abduction and police chase took place in Chino Hills, an upper-middle-class community near the eastern edge of Los Angeles County.

item.title: Todd Blanche’s Loyalty to Trump Is Putting His Attorney General Confirmation at Risk
item.description: Todd Blanche’s approach has collided with the jury-of-two reality in the Senate that has, thus far, kept him from the prize he covets: the stability and status conferred by a Senate confirmation.
item.dc:creator: Glenn Thrush
item.media:description: Todd Blanche, according to current and former officials, understands that coping with President Trump’s demands, rages and U-turns is the price to pay for rising in his orbit.

item.title: Coast Guard Vows to Protect Crews From Brain Injuries Caused by Rough Seas
item.description: The head of the Coast Guard said “decisive action” would be taken so the injuries would be recognized, treated and prevented.
item.dc:creator: Dave Philipps
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: U.S. Coast Guard students training near Cape Disappointment in Washington in 2023.

item.title: How the Michigan Primary Is Dividing Jewish Voters
item.description: U.S. support for Israel is dividing Jewish voters — and reshaping the Democratic Party — ahead of Michigan’s primary on Aug. 4. We traveled to Detroit to meet campaigners on both sides of the issue, and find out how the war in Gaza has shaped their politics, and tested their community.
item.dc:creator: Jeremy Raff, Jeff Perlman and Caroline Kim

item.title: Amid Talk of a Party Switch, Fetterman Vows ‘Never’
item.description: Changing one’s affiliation is rare in the Senate, but it can have big consequences. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania says he is staying put as a Democrat.
item.dc:creator: Carl Hulse
item.media:description: Senator John Fetterman, Democrat of Pennsylvania, at the Capitol this week.

item.title: Gavin Newsom and His Wife Made $1.4 Million in 2024, Tax Returns Show
item.description: The taxable income of California’s governor and his wife, Jennifer Siebel Newsom, exceeded $1 million a year from 2021 to 2024.
item.dc:creator: Tim Arango
item.media:description: The Newsoms released their tax filings as federal agents investigated Jennifer Siebel Newsom’s finances. They said the forms countered right-wing claims that they had enriched themselves while Mr. Newsom was in office.

item.title: Ukraine’s Strike on Iranian Ship Shows How Two Wars Could Spiral
item.description: Iran sent military aid to Russia for its war against Ukraine. Now the question is whether that conflict and the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran are converging.
item.dc:creator: Edward Wong
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine at the U.S. Capitol on Tuesday. Mr. Zelensky has tried to make the case that the wars in the Middle East and in Ukraine have some common elements.

item.title: A Fledgling Food Reviewer’s Battle With Cyclospora
item.description: Christina Hart, 29, started posting reviews on social media in May. Less than two months later, a stomach illness forced her to stop.
item.dc:creator: Madaleine Rubin
item.media:description: Christina Hart in her car where she records her food review videos.

item.title: Missteps Mount in Justice Dept.’s Case Against Minnesota Anti-ICE Protesters
item.description: The problems plaguing the case have not only hurt the government’s chances, lawyers say, but have also undermined the bonds of trust that prosecutors have traditionally enjoyed in court.
item.dc:creator: Alan Feuer and Ernesto Londoño
item.media:description: Nekima Levy Armstrong, center, a local civil rights lawyer, is a lead defendant in the Justice Department’s case against a group of activists and journalists who were arrested over a demonstration at a St. Paul, Minn., church.

item.title: G.O.P. Kills Bid to Expand I.V.F. Access in the Military
item.description: In a notable shift, Republican senators voted unanimously against a proposal to expand the military’s coverage of fertility treatments.
item.dc:creator: Annie Karni
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: Senator Tammy Duckworth, Democrat of Illinois, offered the provision for the defense bill that would have broadened the availability of in vitro fertilization for members of the military.

item.title: CAIR, a Muslim Nonprofit, Gets a Terrorism Label in Florida and Texas
item.description: The federal government designates terrorism groups. But Governors Ron DeSantis and Greg Abbott have gotten in the game, and a focus is CAIR, a nonprofit.
item.dc:creator: Richard Fausset
item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Council on American Islamic Relations in Washington.

item.title: How the Pro-Trump Media Ecosystem Is Splintering Ahead of the Midterms
item.description: Once united in support of President Trump, right-wing influencers are embroiled in feuds and losing viewers, creating a problem for Republicans in the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Stuart A. Thompson

item.title: What Is the Board of Peace? The Trump-Backed Group, Explained.
item.description: President Trump created the international organization, aimed at resolving the long-running war in Gaza and other conflicts.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.media:description: President Trump at a signing ceremony for the founding charter of the Board of Peace at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, in January.

item.title: Kennedy Center Halts Free Public Tours After Five Decades of Service
item.description: The decision to suspend tours came after a volunteer tour guide was featured in a Times article detailing President Trump’s dramatic revamp of the Kennedy Center.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Williamson
item.category: Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:credit: Jared Soares for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Kennedy Center in Washington in June. It has now ended free public tours of the facility.

item.title: Defying Trump, Cornyn Uses His Lame-Duck Power
item.description: In standing in the way of Todd Blanche, President Trump’s choice for attorney general, a liberated Senator John Cornyn is wielding his leverage.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold
item.media:description: Senator John Cornyn in Washington, on Thursday.

item.title: Trump Says Peace Board Has Plan for Gaza Disarmament
item.description: There was no immediate comment from Hamas or Israel, though the Board of Peace said Hamas had agreed to a “road map” to give up its weapons.
item.dc:creator: Katie Rogers and Pranav Baskar
item.media:description: President Trump at the Board of Peace charter announcement at the World Economic Forum, in Davos, Switzerland, in January.

item.title: Alabama Plans Inmate’s Execution After Supreme Court Blocked Last Attempt
item.description: The state will try again to execute Jeffery Lee — this time, by lethal injection — after courts said doing so using nitrogen gas was “likely unconstitutional.”
item.dc:creator: Rick Rojas
item.media:description: Alabama’s lethal injection chamber at the Holman Correctional Facility in Atmore, Ala., around 2002.

item.title: Seattle’s Police Chief Resigns Under Pressure After Festival Shooting
item.description: The decision followed days of criticism over how the department handled the release of information about a shooting that killed three people.
item.dc:creator: Anna Griffin
item.media:description: Chief Shon Barnes of the Seattle Police Department at a vigil for victims of a shooting at the Bite of Seattle food festival.

item.title: Texas Parents Try New Tactic to Remove Ten Commandments From Schools
item.description: A lawsuit filed by three parents argues that the displays violate a state religious freedom law and asks for them to be removed before school starts in August.
item.dc:creator: J. David Goodman

item.media:description: A Ten Commandments poster displayed in a classroom in Fort Worth, Texas.

item.title: Two More Appeals Courts Rule Against Trump’s Detention Policy
item.description: The rulings deepen a split across the judiciary, making it more likely that the Supreme Court will consider the legality of detaining undocumented immigrants indefinitely.
item.dc:creator: Mattathias Schwartz
item.media:credit: Paul Ratje for The New York Times
item.media:description: Large tents meant to house thousands of immigrant detainees at Camp East Montana, a detention facility built at Fort Bliss in El Paso.

item.title: Dulles Airport’s Reviled ‘People Movers’ May Be Lurching Into the Sunset
item.description: A $22.5 billion redesign plan eliminates the “mobile lounges,” which were conceived as a way of making air travel more efficient. Many passengers found the opposite to be true.
item.dc:creator: Sopan Deb
item.media:description: A mobile lounge at Dulles International Airport in Northern Virginia last year.
